context.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a regional insurer's 30-year-old claims platform by gradually migrating claim types to a hybrid cloud architecture while the COBOL/DB2 mainframe remains the system of record.]

## Key Elements
- End Customers & Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- New Claims Platform (Azure West Europe PaaS)
- Legacy Mainframe (On-premise COBOL/DB2)
- Anti-Corruption Layer / Enterprise Messaging Queue
- Active Directory / Identity Provider
- Reconciliation Service & Audit System

## Relationships
- End Customers & Brokers -> New Claims Platform (HTTPS via Web/Mobile UI)
- Claims Adjusters -> New Claims Platform (HTTPS)
- New Claims Platform <-> Legacy Mainframe (Asynchronous messaging via ESB/MQ acting as Anti-Corruption Layer)
- Active Directory <-> New Claims Platform (OpenID Connect / SAML over HTTPS for SSO)

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service & SQL Database: Managed PaaS to reduce cloud management overhead for an inexperienced team
- Enterprise Messaging Queue with Dead-Letter Queues (DLQs): Asynchronous buffering to respect the 23:00-05:00 batch window and protect mainframe connection pools
- OpenID Connect / SAML: Protocol for single sign-on integration with Active Directory
- Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Automates Azure resource provisioning and deployment repeatability

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture decouples the modern cloud frontend from the fragile legacy mainframe via an asynchronous Anti-Corruption Layer, ensuring zero data loss and strict maintainability during the 3-year migration. It isolates expensive mainframe changes while empowering adjusters with a sub-second web experience.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a 30-year-old mainframe claims system by gradually migrating claim types to a hybrid cloud platform while ensuring uninterrupted legacy operations. It enables online claim submissions, modern adjuster workflows, and strict transactional consistency.]

## Key Elements
- **End Customers & Brokers**: External users submitting claims online
- **Claims Adjusters**: Internal users managing claims via a new web application
- **Migration Operations Team**: Users monitoring data reconciliation and rollbacks
- **Azure API Management**: Single entry point handling OIDC/OAuth2 Active Directory SSO
- **Customer Portal & Adjuster Workspace**: React SPAs with a Node.js BFF for performance
- **Claims Core Engine**: Java Spring Boot application for domain logic and claim-type feature flagging
- **Integration Mediator**: Azure Logic Apps/Function App translating events for the legacy mainframe
- **Legacy Mainframe**: COBOL/DB2 on-premise system of record
- **Azure Service Bus**: Enterprise Messaging Queue with Dead-Letter Queues (DLQs)
- **Azure Cosmos DB / PostgreSQL**: Polyglot persistence layer with Change Data Capture (CDC)
- **Migration Operations Dashboard**: Dedicated monitoring and reconciliation UI

## Relationships
- **End Customers/Brokers to Customer Portal**: HTTPS (REST/JSON) via Azure API Management
- **Claims Adjusters to Adjuster Workspace**: HTTPS (REST/JSON) via Azure API Management
- **API Gateway to Node.js BFF & Claims Core**: HTTPS (REST/gRPC)
- **Claims Core to Azure Service Bus**: AMQP
- **Claims Core to Legacy Mainframe**: TCP/MQ via Integration Mediator (JSON-to-COBOL copybook mapping)
- **Persistence to Migration Operations Dashboard**: Change Data Capture (CDC)

## Technology Stack
- **Azure Container Apps (ACA)**: Abstracts infrastructure complexity for a team with low cloud experience
- **Azure API Management**: Enforces Active Directory SSO and centralized OIDC/OAuth2 token validation
- **React SPA & Node.js BFF**: Decouples UI loading times (<2s) from slow mainframe responses
- **Java / Spring Boot**: Robust core business logic execution on containerized runtimes
- **Azure Service Bus**: Ensures reliable message delivery with AMQP, DLQs, and automated replays
- **Terraform / Bicep**: Automated infrastructure provisioning for operational consistency

## Rationale
[The hybrid architecture utilizes Azure Container Apps and managed services to reduce operational overhead for a cloud-novice team while safely bridging modern cloud components to the on-premise mainframe. Decoupled SPAs, feature flagging, and CDC-driven dashboards directly fulfill stringent performance, zero data loss, and rapid rollback requirements.]

Azure API Management.analysis:
## Overview
[Gradually replaces the 30-year-old mainframe claims system of a regional insurer with a modern platform while the legacy system keeps processing claims.]

## Key Elements
* Azure API Management (Standard v2 tier)
* Token Validator Component
* Dynamic Routing Policy Engine
* Transformation & Header Injection Component
* Active Directory / Identity Provider
* Claims Core Engine (Java Spring Boot)
* Integration Mediator (Azure Logic Apps / Function App)
* Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2)
* Azure App Configuration
* Application Insights & Azure Monitor

## Relationships
* End Customers & Brokers -> Azure API Management: Submit claims and interact via HTTPS (REST/JSON)
* Claims Adjusters -> Azure API Management: Manage claims via HTTPS (REST/JSON)
* Azure API Management -> Active Directory / Identity Provider: Validates OAuth2/OIDC tokens via HTTPS
* Azure API Management -> Claims Core Engine: Routes API requests via HTTPS (gRPC)
* Azure API Management -> Integration Mediator: Routes legacy traffic via HTTPS
* Azure API Management -> Azure App Configuration: Fetches Named Values for routing rules via HTTPS

## Technology Stack
* Azure API Management (Standard v2 tier): Balances predictable performance with managed infrastructure for a cloud-novice team
* APIM Policy Fragments & Named Values: Enables dynamic path-based routing and rapid 1-day rollbacks (R-06) without code deployments
* Azure App Configuration: Decouples routing switches from code for secure configuration management
* Azure Bicep: Provides Infrastructure-as-Code to prevent manual configuration drift
* Application Insights & Azure Monitor: Tracks end-to-end latency, error rates, and isolates routing overhead from mainframe responses

## Rationale
[This architecture uses Azure API Management as a unified entry point to securely route traffic, enforce Active Directory SSO, and execute dynamic path-based routing for gradual claim type migration. It ensures business continuity and sub-2-second adjuster screen loads while minimizing operational complexity for a cloud-novice team.]

## Rationale
[This architecture minimizes operational complexity for a cloud-inexperienced team by leveraging managed Azure PaaS services and integrated Next.js capabilities. It guarantees the required sub-2-second performance and supports gradual, risk-controlled claim type migration with rapid fallback options.]

Claims Core Engine.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a hybrid cloud Claims Core Engine built with Java Spring Boot to modernize a regional insurer's claims platform. Its core purpose is to gradually migrate claim types from a 30-year-old mainframe while ensuring continuous processing and data consistency.]

## Key Elements
- Claim Orchestrator (Spring State Machine)
- Feature Router Component (Azure App Configuration)
- Synchronization & Reconciliation Adapter
- Data Access Facade (Spring Data JPA)
- Resilience & Caching Proxy (Resilience4j)
- Telemetry Interceptor (OpenTelemetry)

## Relationships
- Claims Core Engine -> Azure Service Bus: Publishes and consumes asynchronous messages [AMQP]
- Claims Core Engine -> Integration Mediator: Communicates domain events and legacy traffic [TCP/MQ, HTTPS]
- Claims Core Engine -> Polyglot Persistence Layer: Reads and writes claim state [PostgreSQL, Azure Cosmos DB]
- Claims Core Engine -> Azure Key Vault: Retrieves secrets using managed identities [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Java Spring Boot: Core framework for application logic and component wiring
- Spring State Machine: Manages complex claim lifecycles across mixed states
- Resilience4j: Implements circuit breakers to isolate legacy mainframe latency
- OpenTelemetry: Provides distributed tracing across hybrid infrastructure
- Azure App Configuration: Externalizes feature flags for business-driven rollbacks
- Terraform: Manages immutable infrastructure-as-code deployments

## Rationale
[This architecture cleanly separates hybrid integration logic from domain processing using resilient proxies and decoupled event patterns. It guarantees strict performance, consistency, and rapid one-day rollback capabilities despite team cloud inexperience.]

Integration Mediator.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a hybrid cloud-on-premise Insurance Claims Modernization platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe while ensuring zero data loss and uninterrupted business operations.]

## Key Elements
- Business Operations Owner
- Integration Mediator Container
- Routing Router Component (Azure Logic Apps)
- Circuit Breaker & Retry Policy Component (Azure Function middleware)
- Copybook Mapper Component (Azure Functions, Node.js/TypeScript)
- Dead-Letter Handler Component (Azure Functions & Azure Storage Queue)
- Migration Operations Dashboard

## Relationships
- Claims Core Engine -> Routing Router: Domain Events [HTTP/REST or AMQP]
- Routing Router -> Circuit Breaker: Validated Payload [HTTP]
- Circuit Breaker -> Copybook Mapper: Throttled Transformation [Internal Function Call]
- Copybook Mapper -> Legacy Mainframe: COBOL Transaction [TCP/MQ via JSON-to-COBOL copybook mapping]
- Dead-Letter Handler -> Migration Operations Dashboard: Enriched Business Exception [REST/WebSockets with OpenTelemetry correlation ID]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Logic Apps & Azure Functions: Chosen for serverless event routing and lightweight payload transformation given the team's cloud experience level.
- Node.js/TypeScript: Used within Azure Functions for JSON-to-COBOL copybook mapping.
- Azure Service Bus: Provides persistent exponential backpressure and dead-lettering for hybrid queue sinking.
- OpenTelemetry & Azure Monitor Application Insights: Establishes unified distributed tracing across cloud and on-premise components.
- Terraform: Implements Infrastructure-as-Code and GitOps pipeline templates to reduce operational complexity.

## Rationale
[This architecture successfully isolates the fragile, expensive-to-change COBOL/DB2 mainframe behind resilient integration middleware while enabling incremental, low-risk claim type migrations. It strictly satisfies consistency, maintainability, and observability constraints within a hybrid cloud environment.]

Azure Service Bus.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a hybrid cloud insurance claims modernization platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe while ensuring continuous legacy claim processing.]

## Key Elements
- End Customers & Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2)
- Azure API Management
- Customer Portal & Adjuster Workspace (React SPA & Node.js BFF)
- Claims Core Engine (Java Spring Boot)
- Integration Mediator (Azure Logic Apps / Function App)
- Azure Service Bus with Claims Topic, Migration Routing Filters, and Dead-Letter Subscriptions
- Polyglot Persistence Layer (Azure Cosmos DB / PostgreSQL)
- Active Directory / Identity Provider
- Migration Operations Dashboard

## Relationships
- End Customers & Brokers -> Azure API Management: Online claim submission [HTTPS / OIDC]
- Claims Adjusters -> Azure API Management: Adjuster claim handling [HTTPS / OAuth2]
- Azure API Management -> Customer Portal & Adjuster Workspace: Routes frontend traffic [HTTPS]
- Customer Portal & Adjuster Workspace -> Claims Core Engine: API requests [REST / HTTPS]
- Claims Core Engine -> Azure Service Bus: Publishes claims and handles sessions [AMQP over TLS]
- Integration Mediator -> Azure Service Bus: Mediates legacy routing [AMQP over TLS]
- Claims Core Engine & Integration Mediator -> Legacy Mainframe: Data synchronization and batch processing [DB2 / SNA / Batch]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Service Bus: Enterprise messaging backbone chosen for managed reliability, duplicate detection, and Dead-Letter Queues (DLQs).
- React SPA & Node.js BFF: Modern frontend and backend-for-frontend powering adjuster screens and customer portals.
- Java Spring Boot: Core business logic processing container.
- Azure Cosmos DB / PostgreSQL: Polyglot persistence layer for modern data storage.
- Infrastructure as Code (Bicep/Terraform): Automated deployments to mitigate risks from low cloud experience.

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture isolates the legacy mainframe behind managed integration layers while modernizing the user-facing platform with cloud-native components. It guarantees transactional consistency and rapid rollback capabilities necessary for a phased, low-risk migration.]

Polyglot Persistence Layer.analysis:
## Overview
The Polyglot Persistence Layer manages hybrid data storage for the modern claims platform during the 3-year mainframe migration. It provides schema flexibility, strong transactional consistency, and native change data capture to ensure zero data loss.

## Key Elements
- Document Store (Azure Cosmos DB)
- Relational Store (Azure PostgreSQL)
- Managed CDC & Audit Streamer (Azure Event Hubs)
- Claims Core Engine
- Reconciliation Service & Audit System
- Migration Operations Dashboard

## Relationships
- Claims Core Engine -> Document Store (Azure Cosmos DB): HTTPS/TCP via Cosmos SDK for CRUD operations
- Claims Core Engine -> Relational Store (Azure PostgreSQL): TCP/IP via JDBC for transactional consistency
- Document Store & Relational Store -> Managed CDC & Audit Streamer (Azure Event Hubs): Native change streams
- Managed CDC & Audit Streamer -> Reconciliation Service & Audit System (AMQP/HTTPS) for audit logging
- Managed CDC & Audit Streamer -> Migration Operations Dashboard (WebSockets/HTTPS) for real-time tracking

## Technology Stack
- Azure Cosmos DB: Provides schema flexibility for migrating disparate claim types
- Azure PostgreSQL: Delivers strong transactional consistency for core claims data
- Azure Event Hubs: Powers fully managed native change data capture (CDC) to minimize operational toil for an inexperienced cloud team
- OpenTelemetry: Enforces distributed tracing across databases to meet strict sub-2s latency requirements

## Rationale
This polyglot architecture balances schema flexibility for incremental claim type migration with strong transactional consistency and auditability. Utilizing fully managed Azure services mitigates operational risks for a team with limited cloud experience while ensuring robust rollback capabilities.

Migration Operations Dashboard.analysis:
## Overview
The Migration Operations Dashboard provides real-time monitoring and discrepancy detection for the hybrid Insurance Claims Modernization platform. It ensures zero data loss and supports rapid rollback decisions during the phased migration from the legacy mainframe.

## Key Elements
- Migration Leads and Operations Managers (Primary Users)
- Dashboard UI (React SPA)
- Dashboard BFF / API (Node.js/Express)
- Reconciliation Processor (Python/Pandas)
- Compliance & Audit Component (Node.js / Serverless)
- Operations Datastore (Azure PostgreSQL)
- Asynchronous Batch Staging Queue (Azure Blob Storage)

## Relationships
- Migration Leads & Operations Managers -> Dashboard UI: Monitors migration progress and discrepancy alerts via HTTPS/WSS
- Dashboard UI -> Dashboard BFF / API: Fetches aggregated metrics and audit logs via HTTPS/REST/GraphQL
- Dashboard BFF / API -> Operations Datastore: Queries audit logs and discrepancy states via SQL/TLS
- Reconciliation Processor -> Operations Datastore: Persists audit logs and discrepancy states via SQL/TLS
- Reconciliation Processor -> Asynchronous Batch Staging Queue: Buffers mainframe batch dumps via Azure Blob SDK/HTTPS
- Polyglot Persistence Layer -> Reconciliation Processor: Streams real-time updates via Change Data Capture (CDC)

## Technology Stack
- React SPA: Matches the Customer Portal stack to reduce cognitive load for low-cloud-experience teams
- Node.js/Express BFF: Provides familiar backend development patterns matching existing services
- Python/Pandas Reconciliation Processor: Delivers powerful data validation capabilities for cross-system comparisons
- Azure PostgreSQL: Ensures robust relational integrity, audit tracking, and Row-Level Security
- Azure Blob Storage: Buffers heavy mainframe batch extracts during the 23:00-05:00 window to prevent resource contention

## Rationale
This architecture minimizes operational risk by using familiar technologies that align with the team's skillset. It isolates heavy batch workloads while providing reliable, auditable governance to safely manage the hybrid mainframe-to-cloud migration.
